Graduate Program Overview
The Department of Computer Science at Texas Tech University provides an excellent
environment for furthering your studies. Faculty members have research specialties
across the entire spectrum of computer science. You can view the different research groups here or you can view our individual faculty member pages here.
Our department offers five different graduate programs:
Master of Science in Computer Science (MSCS)
Curriculum and Courses
Master of Science in Software and Security Engineering (MSSSE)
Curriculum and Courses
Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science
Curriculum and Courses
Graduate Certificate in Software Engineering
Curriculum and Courses
Graduate Certificate in Security
Curriculum and Courses
The above programs strive to provide students with:
an advanced education in computer science topics,
the ability to pursue specialized subject tracks,
opportunities to work directly with faculty members through research, and
community with like-minded, highly-driven students.
Our graduates have been employed in many top companies including Microsoft, Meta,
LinkedIn, Amazon, Google, Apple, Oracle, VMware, HPE, Nvidia, Dell, Adobe, IBM, NASA,
as well as in the banking industry, investment firms, and other industry sectors.
Our PhD graduates have joined tier-one research universities and teaching universities
as professors and national laboratories as research scientists.
Distance Coursework
Our program offers coursework which can be completed 100% virtually (distance)*, meaning that students can earn a MSCS, MSSSE, or graduate certificate from anywhere.
*Distance courses may have some synchronous, virtual components at the discretion
of the instructor. CS faculty do their best to provide any synchronous requirements
(e.g. exam scheduling, presentations) to students in advance so that they may plan
accordingly. Distance students will NOT be required to come to the Lubbock campus*
Currently, the PhD is not offered virtually.
Transfer Students
Transfer credit may be accepted from another university as long as the following conditions are met:
A final grade of 'B' or higher was earned in the course. Students are required to
submit an official transcript submitted to the Graduate School.
The course was not taken by correspondence.
The inclusion of the course satisfies degree plan requirements.
The course is approved by the Graduate Advisor, Graduate Coordinator, and (if applicable)
the student's thesis advisor.
A Texas Tech University course corresponds to the transferred course.
The course is from a computer science or similar program.
A MS student may only transfer up to 6 hours (two classes). Students should be prepared
to provide transfer coursework syllabi. PhD students wishing to transfer coursework
should speak to their research advisor for additional information.
Interested in applying? Start here.
Have questions? Contact our CS Grad Advising Team! We're happy to help!
General inquires can be sent to cs.grad_advisor@ttu.edu
Prospective students are welcome to schedule an appointment with advisor using Calendly.
